intended_object: The restriction μ|_s of a measure μ to a set s, i.e. the measure t ↦ μ(t ∩ s) on measurable sets t (from the docstring and name).
explanation: The definition is `restrictₗ s μ`. Here `restrictₗ s` is built with `liftLinear` from the outer-measure restriction `OuterMeasure.restrict s`. This lift sends μ to the measure induced by the outer measure t ↦ μ(t ∩ s), and the accompanying proof shows that every μ-measurable set is Carathéodory-measurable for that outer measure. So for every measurable t, `μ.restrict s t = μ (t ∩ s)`, which is the standard restriction of a measure. Since this uses the outer measure, the construction also works when s is not measurable, which is a harmless generalization. It is defined for an arbitrary measurable space, so the generality is right. This is Mathlib's own canonical definition of measure restriction, and Mathlib has no other declaration for the same object.
